messages:
ben: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a sustained spike in tokens/sec and a drop in batch_util on two GPU pools since ~1715032000. KV cache hitrate also dipped ~8%. Pushed a short profile to GCS: gs://redwood-perf/1715032468/profile.pb.gz :eyes:

alex: link? which pools?

ben: pools: rwd-dedicated-eu-1 and rwd-dedicated-eu-2. Here's the grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/batching?orgId=1&fullscreen

infra-bot: [ALERT] batch_utilization_p95 < 30% for rwd-dedicated-eu-1 (duration 12m)

maria: hmm — we rolled the kernel-selector canary at 1715029000 that prefers fused-attn on step lengths <=128. Could be falling back unexpectedly for longer seqs and causing more token churn?

ben: profile shows a lot of time in queueing_work (continuous-batcher) and threads spinning on queue_wakeup. Snippet: ```text
# top stacks
continuous_batcher::form_batch  42%
kernel_selector::choose 18%
kv_cache::lookup 12%
rpc::send 8%
```

alex: kv_cache hitrate drop could be from new canary that changed prefix hashing? maria any config touched?

maria: no hash changes. I did change the kernel scoring function to penalize kernels with >30% mem-copy for long sequences. Maybe scoring influences placement and we get worse cache locality.

taylor: we should confirm whether queueing policy moved more short requests to other GPUs (fragmentation). Can we add a quick telemetry panel: per-host batch_util, per-model kv_hitrate, tokens_per_sec, and microburst_count (requests/s sampled at 1s)? I'll add briefly to dashboard.

sre-oncall: please also add a rolling alert on tokens/sec deviation (>30% from baseline) and queue_depth_p95 > 1.5x baseline. We had a customer-facing latency blip.

ben: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) revert kernel-selector change on canary hosts (maria?) 2) reduce continuous-batcher max_wait from 12ms -> 8ms for those pools (taylor?) 3) enable more aggressive prefix KV caching sampling (alex?)

maria: I can rollback the selector on canary hosts now. Doing `kubectl -n runtime set image kernel-selector=registry/redwood/kernel-selector:stable-2026-02-14` and watch.

alex: I'll flip sampling on KV cache: set env KV_CACHE_SAMPLE_RATE=0.20 for the pools and deploy.

taylor: I added a temporary grafana row (panel ids): batch_util_pct (panel 211), queue_depth_p95 (212), tokens_per_sec (213), kv_hitrate_by_model (214), microburst_count_1s (215). Also created an ad-hoc log link to the profile: https://logs.redwood.com/q/1715032468

ben: after rolling back the selector on two hosts and bumping cache sampling I see batch_util jump from 22% -> 46% within 3 min, tokens/sec stabilizing. Leaving the reduced max_wait off until we confirm.

maria: good catch — the penalty for mem-copy was too aggressive. I'll revert that scoring change and run an ablation test in staging with longer seq distribution.

sre-oncall: Notes for postmortem: record the selector change, telemetry gaps (no microburst_count previously), actions taken and rollback timestamp. Add an alert for kv_hitrate_delta > 5% over 10m.

ben: Action items: 
- maria: revert scoring and run staging ablation (ETA 24h)
- alex: KV cache sampling change rolled; follow up with metrics for hitrate per-model (ETA 4h)
- taylor: keep the temporary panels for 48h and create a dashboard template for batch-health (ETA 1d)
- sre-oncall: draft postmortem doc and SLA impact calc (ETA 48h)

maria: started the revert, will update when staging run finishes.

ben: thanks all. TL;DR: kernel-selector scoring regression -> worse placement -> KV cache locality drop -> lower batch_util -> higher tokens/sec and queueing. Dashboards/panels added, rollback worked. We'll tighten the canary gating to include kv_hitrate + batch_util smoke checks next deploy. :thumbsup:
